- **Plant:** Tomato (*Solanum lycopersicum*), confirmed by the characteristic serrated/lobed leaves
- **Affected part:** Stem, specifically at/near a nodal junction
- **Key features:**
  - Large, extensive **brown-to-tan dry necrotic canker** girdling the stem
  - Canker appears sunken, corky, and dry in texture
  - Located at a branch/node junction
  - Associated yellowing of a nearby leaf (visible upper-left)
  - No white mycelium or sclerotia visible (rules out Sclerotinia, Southern Blight)
  - No water-soaked appearance (less consistent with early Phytophthora Blight)
  - No visible dark sporulation masses or fruit symptoms

| **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers** | Strong — Alternaria causes dry, dark-brown girdling stem cankers, especially at nodes/leaf attachment points on tomato |
| Phytophthora_Blight | Moderate — stem lesions occur but typically start water-soaked and show darker coloration |
| Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato | Moderate — stem cankers occur but often with more open, oozing lesions and bird's-eye fruit spots |
| Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot | Low — would show white cottony mycelium and black sclerotia |
| Southern_Blight | Low — basal/soil-line disease with white mycelium |

The dry, extensive brown canker at the nodal region, with associated leaf yellowing and no mycelial growth, best matches **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**.
